Explain what DNS does when you open a website to someone with no technical background.
Limits: at most 170 words. Include one analogy, on a line starting with 'Analogy:', and one worked example, on a line starting with 'Example:'. Mention the IP address.
Answer with the explanation only.

arguments.answer:
When you type a website name like "example.com", your computer can't use that name directly. Computers find each other using numbers called IP addresses, such as 93.184.216.34. DNS (Domain Name System) is the service that turns the name you typed into the right IP address, so your computer knows where to go.

Analogy: DNS works like your phone's contacts list. You tap "Mom" and the phone looks up her number and dials it, so you never have to remember the digits.

Example: You type "example.com" into your browser. Your computer asks a DNS server, "What's the address for example.com?" The server replies, "93.184.216.34." Your browser then connects to that IP address and the page loads. This all happens in a split second.

Your computer usually saves the answer for a while. The next time you visit, it can skip the lookup and the page can load faster. Without DNS, you would have to memorize a string of numbers for every website you use.
